newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal sues Champion over patent.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal sues Champion over patent.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc sued Champion Ignition Products in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, alleging that Champion's process for making platinum electrodes for spark plugs infringes an Allied patent in use since 1990.
In court papers made available Thursday, Allied said its process cost millions of dollars to develop and allowed "enormous cost savings through the use of less platinum."
Allied sells tens of millions of the spark plugs and "has a contract to supply a major American automobile manufacturer" worth "tens of millions of dollars," court papers say.
Champion, of Toledo, Ohio, is the successor of Champion Spark Plug Co.

Allied, which alleged that Champion began using its process in 1995, has asked for a court order stopping Champion from further alleged infringement and damages tripled for alleged willful infringement.
